# K-210 Plant Air Compressor: Start, Stop and Protection

## 1. Scope and Equipment

K-210 is a three-stage integrally geared centrifugal air compressor driven by a 900 kW, 6.6 kV motor with a soft starter. Capacity is controlled by inlet guide vanes (IGV: command ZC-210, position ZT-210) and blow-off valve FV-211 to atmosphere. Lube oil is supplied by a shaft-driven main oil pump and an AC auxiliary oil pump P-212. The unit is started and stopped from the DCS by the operator. Discharge header pressure is controlled at 7.0 barg.

Values marked **[TBC]** are not in the supplied data and must be confirmed with the vendor or during commissioning.

## 2. Instrument Summary

| Tag | Service | Values |
|---|---|---|
| PT-213 | Oil header pressure | Normal 2.5 bar; low alarm 1.8 bar; low-low trip 1.3 bar |
| TT-214 | Oil temperature | Start permissive > 25 °C; tank heater available |
| VT-215/216/217 | Vibration, stages 1/2/3 | Alarm 40 µm; trip 60 µm |
| ZT-210 / ZC-210 | IGV position / command | Closed-position feedback used as start permissive |
| FV-211 | Blow-off valve | Open for start, stop, surge and trip |
| P-212 | AC auxiliary oil pump | Pre-lube, post-lube and standby |

## 3. Start Permissives

The DCS shall display each permissive and its status. The start command is accepted only when all are healthy:

1. No active trip, and all trips reset by the operator.
2. Oil temperature TT-214 > 25 °C. If lower, the tank heater is enabled automatically and the start is blocked until the temperature is reached.
3. Auxiliary oil pump P-212 available (not in fault or locked out).
4. IGV at the start position (closed or minimum) per ZT-210.
5. Blow-off valve FV-211 fully open (or commanded open and confirmed).
6. Motor start limits satisfied (section 4).
7. 6.6 kV breaker/starter ready, no motor protection lockout, soft starter healthy.
8. All vibration transmitters VT-215/216/217 healthy (no signal fault).
9. Machine at rest (zero speed or motor current off), to prevent a restart while rotating. **[TBC]** speed source.
10. No active trip from vendor controller. Cooling water available if the intercoolers and oil cooler require it. **[TBC]**

## 4. Motor Start Limits

- Maximum 3 starts per hour.
- Minimum 20 min between hot starts.

The DCS shall keep a start counter in a rolling 60 min window and a timer since the last start. If either limit is violated, the start permissive is withheld and the DCS shows the remaining time before a start is allowed. A start attempt that trips counts as a start. The limits shall not be bypassed from the operator screen; any override needs a password-protected engineering action. **[TBC]** Define "hot" with the motor vendor (for example, a time or temperature threshold since the last run). Until then, treat any start within 20 min of the previous start as a hot start.

## 5. Start Sequence

1. **Operator start command** from the DCS, with permissives healthy. The sequence status is "Starting".
2. **Pre-lube.** Start P-212. PT-213 must reach at least the normal operating value (2.5 bar) within a set time (**[TBC]**, typically 30 to 60 s) and be held for a pre-lube period (**[TBC]**, vendor). If PT-213 does not reach the pressure within the time, abort the start, stop P-212 and alarm "Pre-lube failure".
3. **Confirm FV-211 open and IGV at start position.**
4. **Motor start.** Issue the start command to the soft starter. The soft starter ramps the motor per its settings. Monitor for:
   - Motor reaching full speed within the soft starter ramp time plus margin. If not, trip "Failed to start".
   - PT-213 above the low-low trip setting at all times. Low-low trip protection is active during starting.
   - Vibration alarm and trip active (a vendor-specified start-up delay or higher setpoint during the run-up may apply **[TBC]**; do not mask the trip without vendor agreement).
5. **Run-up complete.** Motor at full speed, bypass contactor closed if applicable. The shaft-driven main oil pump now supplies the lube oil. Once PT-213 is stable at 2.5 bar or above, with a short time delay, P-212 may be stopped and set to standby (auto-start on low pressure). **[TBC]** The vendor may require P-212 to run through a warm-up period.
6. **Warm-up / idle.** The machine runs unloaded with FV-211 open and IGV at minimum for the vendor-specified time (**[TBC]**).
7. **Loading.** The operator selects "Load" (or the sequence continues automatically). Then:
   - Capacity control takes over: the IGV opens and FV-211 closes on a ramp, while the surge controller remains in command of FV-211.
   - Once FV-211 is closed and the IGV is under control, the pressure controller is released to hold the discharge header at 7.0 barg.
   - Loading is by a ramp so that the discharge pressure does not step the header and the machine does not enter surge.
8. **Running.** The status is "Running".

If any step does not complete within its time, the sequence aborts and the machine stops through the normal stop (or a trip if it is already running and the cause is a protective condition).

## 6. Normal Stop

1. **Operator stop command** from the DCS. The status is "Stopping".
2. **Unload.** Ramp the IGV to minimum and open FV-211 so the machine is unloaded and the header is isolated by the check valve. The unload ramp avoids surge and a sudden header pressure change.
3. **Cool-down or idle run** for the vendor-specified time (**[TBC]**), if required.
4. **Stop the motor** with the soft starter, after unload is confirmed (ZT-210 at minimum, FV-211 open). Starting P-212 before the motor stop is recommended so that oil pressure is continuous during coast-down.
5. **Post-lube.** P-212 runs during coast-down until zero speed is confirmed, then for a post-lube period (**[TBC]**, vendor), and then stops. The shaft-driven pump loses pressure as the machine decelerates, so P-212 must start at the motor stop command at the latest.
6. Status returns to "Stopped". The start-limit timers continue to run.

The operator may cancel the stop during the unload step only. The stop command cannot be cancelled once the motor stop has been issued.

## 7. Protection

### 7.1 Alarms and trips

| Condition | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Oil pressure low (PT-213) | < 1.8 bar | Alarm. **Auto-start P-212** if not running. |
| Oil pressure low-low (PT-213) | < 1.3 bar | **Trip** (see 7.2). Delay of a few seconds to avoid nuisance trips from transients **[TBC]**. Use 2oo3 voting if three transmitters are installed; with a single PT-213, ensure it is a SIL-appropriate or well-maintained device. |
| Oil temperature low (TT-214) | < 25 °C before start | Start blocked, heater on. |
| Oil temperature high (TT-214) | **[TBC]** | Alarm and trip, per vendor. |
| Vibration high (VT-215/216/217) | > 40 µm | Alarm, identifying the stage. |
| Vibration high-high | > 60 µm | **Trip.** |
| Surge | Vendor surge line | Open FV-211 (see 7.3). |
| Motor protection | Per relay | Trip, from the motor protection relay (overcurrent, earth fault, thermal, and so on). |
| Emergency stop | Hardwired | Trip. |
| Failed to start or overlong run-up | **[TBC]** | Trip. |
| Discharge pressure/temperature high, stage temperatures | **[TBC]** | Alarm and trip, per vendor. |

### 7.2 Trip action

On any trip:

1. Stop the motor immediately (open the breaker or starter contactor via the hardwired trip path).
2. Open FV-211 fully.
3. Drive the IGV to minimum (closed).
4. Start P-212 for coast-down lubrication (unless the trip is oil related and P-212 is not available, in which case alarm that the coast-down is unlubricated and inform the operator). For a low-low oil pressure trip, still start P-212, because it may restore pressure during coast-down.
5. Latch the first-out cause, time-stamped, and show it on the DCS.
6. Block restart until the operator has acknowledged and reset the trip, the cause has cleared, and the start limits (section 4) are satisfied. After a vibration trip, require a confirmed reset and inspection before restart. **[TBC]** per site rules.

Vibration trip logic: the trip is by any one of the three transmitters above 60 µm, with a short confirmation delay. If the vendor or site policy requires, use 2oo3 voting with transmitter-fault bypass. **[TBC]** With a single transmitter per stage, there is no redundancy, so a failed transmitter results in an alarm and a start block, not a silent bypass.

Trips shall be implemented in the vendor control panel or a safety PLC, independent of the DCS control loops, with the DCS receiving status and first-out indication. The oil pressure and vibration trip signals shall be hardwired to the motor breaker trip circuit.

### 7.3 Surge protection

The vendor controller holds the surge line. When the operating point reaches the surge control line:

1. The controller opens FV-211 to keep the machine away from surge. The surge response overrides the pressure controller and the IGV capacity command.
2. If surge continues, or the operating point crosses the surge (trip) line, FV-211 is opened further and quickly.
3. A repeated surge event count within a set time (**[TBC]**) trips the machine.
4. After the machine is clear of the surge line plus a margin, FV-211 closes slowly under the pressure controller.

FV-211 shall fail open on loss of air or signal. **[TBC]** Confirm the fail position. Blow-off to atmosphere also provides unloaded operation when header demand is low, so the pressure controller and the surge controller must be coordinated to prevent hunting between IGV and FV-211.

### 7.4 Auxiliary oil pump P-212 logic

- Auto-start: on PT-213 < 1.8 bar (alarm), on any trip, and on any motor stop command.
- Pre-lube: runs before every start.
- Selector: Auto (default), Manual On, Manual Off. In Manual Off, a start permissive is withheld.
- P-212 remains running until the oil pressure is stable on the shaft-driven pump and the post-lube period is done.
- If P-212 fails to build the pressure on start, alarm "Aux oil pump fault".

## 8. Open Items to Confirm

1. Define hot start and the motor vendor's time or temperature criterion.
2. Pre-lube, warm-up, cool-down and post-lube times.
3. Whether PT-213, VT-215/216/217 trips need redundancy (voting) given the risk assessment.
4. Vibration trip masking or delay during run-up.
5. FV-211 fail position, and IGV start position.
6. Oil high-temperature, stage temperature, discharge pressure and temperature limits.
7. Zero-speed detection source.
8. Cooling water permissive.
9. Surge repeat count and timing.
